correctness.rationale: For every integer base b≥2 and repunit length r≥4, cyclic carrying modulo M=(b^r−1)/(b−1) reduces any nonzero residue-zero power multiset to a nonzero base-b r-digit numeral jM, 1≤j≤b−1, decreasing weight by b−1 each step. The reverse split increases weight by b−1 without changing residue; putting counts at exponents i+rh makes an actual positive numeral with distinct unit digits. Therefore the spectrum is exactly ⋃_{j=1}^{b−1}(rj+(b−1)ℕ₀). Reducing by gcd d of r and b−1 to coprime a=r/d and c=(b−1)/d yields the c residue classes and floor-sum genus (a−1)(c+1)/2, last relative gap dc(a−1), and conductor d[c(a−1)+1], including a=1 and c=1. Independent residue-state recurrence compared 1,248 bounded weight decisions; finite checks do not prove the all-parameter result.
residual_risks: The theorem excludes r≤3 by claim scope despite the analogous cyclic-carry technique extending to those values.
The relative Frobenius terminology is only for the positive d-lattice; ordinary complement infinite when d>1.
